original_question: Let (W1,S1) and (W2,S2) be Coxeter systems, let J1 subseteq S1 and J2 subseteq S2, let u,v in W1^{J1} and w,z in W2^{J2}, and let f : [u,v] -> [w,z] be a poset isomorphism such that f([u,v]^{J1}) = [w,z]^{J2}. Must the parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials satisfy P_{u,v}^{J1,q}(q) = P_{w,z}^{J2,q}(q)?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Conjecture 1.6: the deeper parabolic generalization of the combinatorial invariance conjecture proposed by Marietti. ([cmtp.uniroma2.it](https://www.cmtp.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s official target almost verbatim: it uses two Coxeter systems, parabolic subsets J1 and J2, elements u,v in W1^{J1} and w,z in W2^{J2}, a poset isomorphism f:[u,v]→[w,z], the crucial condition f([u,v]^{J1})=[w,z]^{J2}, and the type-q conclusion P^{J1,q}_{u,v}(q)=P^{J2,q}_{w,z}(q). It also correctly captures the stronger Marietti conjecture rather than the naive parabolic analogue that the paper says is false in general. ([cmtp.uniroma2.it](https://www.cmtp.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: Define W^J explicitly, as the left quotient/minimal-length representatives of W_J\W; the paper writes W^J={x in W : D_L(x) subseteq S\J}. ([cmtp.uniroma2.it](https://www.cmtp.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Define [a,b]^J explicitly as [a,b]∩W^J={x in W^J : a<=x<=b}; otherwise the distinguished subposets in the hypothesis are implicit. ([cmtp.uniroma2.it](https://www.cmtp.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf?utm_source=openai))
Specify that [u,v] and [w,z] are Bruhat intervals and that f is an isomorphism of posets for Bruhat order. ([cmtp.uniroma2.it](https://www.cmtp.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Fix the normalization of P^{J,q}_{x,y}(q): these are Deodhar’s type-q parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials, a uniquely determined family in Z[q]. ([cmtp.uniroma2.it](https://www.cmtp.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf?utm_source=openai))

If one wants the problem fully stand-alone from the paper, one should mention the theorem-definition data that characterize these polynomials, especially the degree bound deg P^{J,x}_{u,v} < (1/2) l(u,v) for u<v and the defining recursion involving the parabolic R-polynomials over [u,v]^J. ([cmtp.uniroma2.it](https://www.cmtp.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Make the quantifier fully explicit: the question is whether the stated equality holds for every such choice of Coxeter systems, parabolic subsets, endpoints, and interval isomorphism f. ([cmtp.uniroma2.it](https://www.cmtp.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf?utm_source=openai))

For complete paper-faithfulness, note that the paper also records an equivalent formulation with type -1 parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials (and similarly with parabolic R-polynomials). ([cmtp.uniroma2.it](https://www.cmtp.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Is it true that for every pair of Coxeter systems (W1,S1) and (W2,S2), every pair of subsets J1 subseteq S1 and J2 subseteq S2, and every u,v in W1^{J1}, w,z in W2^{J2} (where W_i^{J_i} denotes the left quotient, i.e. the set of minimal-length representatives of W_{J_i}\W_i), if f:[u,v]→[w,z] is a Bruhat-poset isomorphism such that f([u,v]^{J1})=[w,z]^{J2}, where [a,b]^{J}:=[a,b]∩W^{J}, then the type-q parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials in Deodhar’s normalization satisfy P^{J1,q}_{u,v}(q)=P^{J2,q}_{w,z}(q)? ([cmtp.uniroma2.it](https://www.cmtp.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf?utm_source=openai))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, under the same hypotheses, must the type -1 parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials satisfy P^{J1,-1}_{u,v}(q)=P^{J2,-1}_{w,z}(q)? ([cmtp.uniroma2.it](https://www.cmtp.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: The draft is already very strong because it lands on exactly the right conjecture: Conjecture 1.6, not the earlier ordinary CIC and not the naive parabolic analogue that the paper explicitly says fails in general. The nearby paper context needed to make it fully stand-alone is supplied by the definition of the quotient W^J and by Theorem 1.3, which fixes the normalization and degree condition for the type-q parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials. No extra field, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic clause belongs to this problem in the paper; the real omissions are the Bruhat-order interpretation of the intervals, the definitions of W^J and [u,v]^J, and the precise normalization of P^{J,q}_{u,v}(q). ([cmtp.uniroma2.it](https://www.cmtp.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf?utm_source=openai))
